note: a waiting train leaves this long after the reference event (crossing: other train arrives / passes; overtake: overtaker at the next block point; see wait_gaps for per-line overtake gaps)
a planned wait is at least this long (arrival + 1 min)
follower leaves the previous station this long before the train ahead leaves the next (full) station when it continues on the same path

the user may edit any scheduled train (its GAPEKA times are the starting point; the planner re-plans it); scheduled trains are never moved to make room for a train created outside the schedule (it yields and waits, like a KLB held so regular trains stay on time); the train being planned yields to all others
single track: one train per block between two open stations (0 overlaps in GAPEKA 2026); halts are not block points; during dinas tutup the closed stations are not block points either

value: station with a usable Roman track
note: a train can wait only at a station (not a halt) with a Roman track usable in its direction and long enough, unless no other train enters or passes while it stands there (stop alone rule)
gaps between trains are checked with this tolerance: GAPEKA plans in whole minutes and often keeps exactly the minimum gap, while computed running times have seconds

double track: a train may run into the next block only when the train ahead has cleared it; block points = stations (not halts) + the block signals of the track in this direction (sections.block_signals); times inside a block by distance between the train's times at the halts in it; no fixed margin (GAPEKA 2026: 0.0 min beyond block clear at whole minutes), only time_tolerance. Where the sheet shows too few signals (Gambir - Manggarai) a pair is also allowed when spaced at every block point like the tightest GAPEKA pair on that block (headways.double_block_spacing_s)

a FASTER train behind must find each block clear when it passes the block point before it (it sees the signal aspect from there and is not slowed: the user's rule that the slower train stops where continuing would hold up the faster one); 0 = only the block ahead: KRL same-station waits 55 -> 35 %, commuter 48 -> 40 %

double track, same direction: the follower may run into a block only when the block is clear PLUS this dispatcher gap, like single-track operation (user).
